statements.notes: Agent runs every stage itself, back to back, in one session
statements.quote: you run all five stages yourself, back to back, in this session.

statements.notes: The chain takes precedence over any other procedure
statements.quote: This chain is how the task gets solved, and it takes precedence over any procedure you would follow otherwise.

statements.notes: Do not modify Spec Kit's own files
statements.quote: The files under `/tmp/speckit-sdd/.specify/scripts/`, `templates/` and `memory/` are Spec Kit's own; leave them as they are.

statements.notes: Specify creates FEATURE_DIR
statements.quote: The feature directory does not exist yet: the specify stage creates it.

statements.notes: Outputs of the specify stage
statements.quote: | 1 | specify | `/speckit-sdd/stages/01-specify.md` | none; the stage sets the feature up itself | `spec.md`, `checklists/requirements.md` (and `/tmp/speckit-sdd/.specify/feature.json`) |

statements.notes: Script the plan stage runs
statements.quote: | 2 | plan | `/speckit-sdd/stages/02-plan.md` | `setup-plan.sh --json` |

statements.notes: data-model.md and quickstart.md are always created
statements.quote: `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `quickstart.md` (both always; body `N/A — <reason>` when nothing applies)

statements.notes: When nothing applies, the body is N/A with a reason
statements.quote: body `N/A — <reason>` when nothing applies

statements.notes: Contract files must be listed in plan.md's tree, or the tree has an N/A line and no file exists
statements.quote: contract files under `contracts/` (listed in plan.md's Documentation tree, or `contracts/  # N/A — <reason>` there and no file)

statements.notes: Tasks runs its script and produces tasks.md
statements.quote: | 3 | tasks | `/speckit-sdd/stages/03-tasks.md` | `setup-tasks.sh --json` | `tasks.md` |

statements.notes: Script the implement stage runs
statements.quote: `check-prerequisites.sh --json --require-tasks --include-tasks`

statements.notes: Test-first order for each user story
statements.quote: per user story, first its verification scripts in `checks/` (run, seen failing), then the code change in `/testbed`, then the scripts again (passing)

statements.notes: Implement marks completed tasks with [X]
statements.quote: `[X]` marks in `tasks.md`

statements.notes: Converge runs its script and writes the convergence report
statements.quote: `check-prerequisites.sh --json --require-spec --require-tasks --include-tasks` | `convergence.md` (round 2: `convergence-2.md`), and possibly a new Convergence phase in `tasks.md`

statements.notes: Open each stage's document before starting that stage
statements.quote: Begin every stage by opening its document, and carry the stage out from that document rather than from memory.

statements.notes: Each runs once, in order
statements.quote: specify, plan and tasks run once each, in that order.

statements.notes: No more than two rounds
statements.quote: implement and converge then alternate, in at most two rounds

statements.notes: Round 1 covers the whole of tasks.md
statements.quote: Round 1: implement works through the whole of `tasks.md`; converge writes `convergence.md`.

statements.notes: Round 2 is conditional on tasks_appended
statements.quote: If that report's **Outcome** is `tasks_appended`, round 2 follows: implement does only the unchecked tasks (the new `## Phase N: Convergence`), and converge writes `convergence-2.md`.

statements.notes: Stopping condition, then call finish
statements.quote: The chain is over as soon as a converge round records `converged`, or after round 2 whatever it found. Then call `finish`.

statements.notes: The issue text is the feature reference
statements.quote: The issue in the task message ... is the feature description for the specify stage and stays the reference for every later stage.
Use only that text, the repository and what is already installed.

statements.notes: Do not fetch links; mark the ones that matter as unverified
statements.quote: Links in the issue stay closed (where one matters, note it as `[UNVERIFIED — not fetched]`)
nothing is searched for online, and no package is installed.

statements.notes: A message without a tool call ends the session
statements.quote: go from one stage straight into the next; a stage ends by opening the next document, not with a summary;

statements.notes: Never ask questions; record decisions instead
statements.quote: if you catch yourself about to ask something, decide it instead: take the most plausible reading and write it down where it belongs (the spec's `## Assumptions`, a decision in `research.md`, the notes of `checklists/requirements.md`);

statements.notes: A tracking tool is optional (may) but cannot replace the checkboxes
statements.quote: the checkboxes in `tasks.md` are the record of implement's progress; a task-tracking tool is optional scratch beside them, never a substitute.

statements.notes: Not changed after specify
statements.quote: | `spec.md`, `checklists/requirements.md` | specify | no |

statements.notes: Not changed after plan
statements.quote: | `plan.md`, `research.md`, Phase 1 files | plan | no |

statements.notes: Only these two kinds of later change are allowed
statements.quote: | `tasks.md` | tasks | only by implement's `[X]` marks and by converge appending a `## Phase N: Convergence` |

statements.notes: One report per round; not changed later
statements.quote: | `convergence.md`, `convergence-2.md` | converge, one per round | no |
| `checks/` | implement, for the verification scripts of the test tasks; any stage, for scratch files | as needed |
implement is the only stage that edits `/testbed`; the other stages only read it and run commands in it.
No test file is added or changed there.
The tests this workflow writes are the verification scripts in `FEATURE_DIR/checks/`: each is run and seen failing before the code it covers exists, and passing once it does.
The existing tests related to the change are run before implementing, for a baseline, and again afterwards.
Ignore files (`.gitignore`, `.dockerignore` and so on) stay untouched.
Nothing of the workflow lands in `/testbed`: no spec copies, notes, summaries or scratch scripts. All of that belongs in `FEATURE_DIR`
with verification scripts and scratch files under `FEATURE_DIR/checks/`. A script written anywhere else — `/tmp/test_x.py`, `/testbed/repro.py` — breaks this rule.
